parsed.same_study_reason: Both lists critique a global machine-learning map of natural forest regeneration potential. Both mention labels derived from Fagan et al. regrowth data, Global Forest Watch/GFC inputs, biophysical versus socioeconomic predictors and headline area estimates (215 Mha).

pairs.reason: Both criticise the outcome definition of regrowth. A1 says the >5 m height threshold misses early or slow regeneration and persistence; B1 says it ignores intensive-margin recovery within existing forest.
Both target the inherited regrowth definition. A1 faults the height threshold and persistence; B8 faults classifying all non-plantation gain as natural, conflating it with assisted regeneration.
Both question whether the validation shows true predictive performance. A2 cites non-spatially-blocked random splits; B2 cites validating future predictions against past outcomes.
Both argue reported model performance is overstated. A2 attributes this to spatial autocorrelation in random splits; B3 to leakage from contemporaneous predictors.

Both cite omission errors and low producer's accuracy in the Fagan et al. regrowth labels, which create false negatives. A3 stresses biased training patterns, B5 stresses an overstated available area including already-regrown land.
Both note that socioeconomic predictors are dropped from the predictive model, so biophysical variables proxy for human factors. Hence the outputs cannot be read as purely biophysical potential.

Both say the model fails to isolate biophysical potential from human land-use influence. A9 attributes this to sampling non-regeneration points from managed or cleared lands, B4 to confounding when socioeconomic variables are dropped.

Both concern temporal misalignment between predictors and the 2000–2016 outcome period. A7 stresses inconsistency and transfer problems from 2018 covariates; B3 stresses leakage from contemporaneous predictors inflating performance.
Both raise Global Forest Watch/GFC data versions. A7 worries about inconsistency across mixed versions and years; B7 says an outdated GFC gain version was used despite improved releases.

Both discuss the temporal windows of predictors such as NPP and burned area. A8 is concerned with mixed resolutions producing false precision at 30 m, B3 with leakage from overlap with the outcome period.
Both target the headline expected-area estimate. A12 says its confidence intervals omit major uncertainty sources; B6 says it is far above the Fagan benchmark and lacks a hindcast validation.
Both question the headline 215 Mha area estimate. A12 faults underestimated uncertainty, partly from label noise; B5 argues the area is biased upward by including already-regrown land.
Both touch on validating how probabilities translate into area estimates. A11 asks about calibration and precision/recall, B6 about a hindcast benchmark comparison.
